steps.u: The daily revenue dbt model got slow, 40 minutes now. Make it fast again.

steps.r: select ... from orders o join order_items i on ... join customers c on ... where date(o.created_at) = date(current_date - 1)

steps.a: The filter wraps the timestamp column in a function, which prevents partition pruning, so the whole orders table is scanned every day. A range predicate on the raw column lets the warehouse prune partitions, and the model can be incremental.

i.new_string: where o.created_at >= current_date - 1 and o.created_at < current_date

reference.summary: Cut a dbt revenue model from 40 minutes to about two by replacing a function wrapped date filter with a range predicate so partitions can be pruned and making the model incremental; dbt tests pass.
facts: function on the filter column blocked partition pruning

decisions.choice: use a range predicate on the raw timestamp
decisions.reason: a function around the column prevents partition pruning and forces a full scan
